fields.title: Activation: the moment after which a person stays
fields.keyTakeaway: A product usually has an action after which churn drops sharply. Onboarding's job is to get users to it as fast as possible, not to show every feature.
fields.checkQuestion: How do you find Reestr's aha moment without asking users?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **how to turn leads into active users?**
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you do not answer the question.** Onboarding turns into a feature tour: six screens that users swipe through. There are signups, but no payments.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: Found in data, not made up
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **Action hypotheses** — what a person could do in the first few days: created a document, invited a colleague, signed.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Cohort comparison** — how retention differs between those who did it and those who did not.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Threshold** — often it is not just the action that matters, but the count: not "created a document", but "created three in the first week".
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Causality test** — correlation is not causation. Tested by intentionally driving people to perform the action and checking if retention changes.
fields.blocks/3/text:
Hypotheses: created an invoice, signed a document, invited an accountant.

Retention after 30 days:
created an invoice — 34%;
signed a document — 51%;
invited an accountant — 78%.

Inviting an accountant looks strongest, but only 6% do it — likely because they are simply the most serious clients.

Tested: added an "invite accountant" step to onboarding and raised the share from 6% to 23%. Retention in this group was 61%: lower than 78%, but noticeably higher than average. This means a connection exists, but part of the effect was selection, not causation.
fields.blocks/3/title: Reestr, what was found in the data
fields.blocks/4/text: Every extra step before the first value drops some users. Good onboarding removes friction — auto-filling, pre-populating examples, skipping optional steps — rather than adding explanations.
fields.blocks/5/text: An aha moment is a property of a segment, not of the entire product. For Reestr users who are sole proprietors without employees, it is creating an invoice, while inviting an accountant makes no sense: they do not have an accountant.
